Review every query/branch and all represented source obligations. No fixtures, labels, counterpart records, expected verdicts or known solution are supplied. Never request them. Shape messages and execution success are not proofs of correct logic.

The packet supplies full_candidate once. Use candidate_location rather than quoting code: {candidate_version, candidate_sha256, unit: "lines" or "characters", start, end}. Lines are one-based inclusive; character offsets are zero-based half-open Unicode positions. The server extracts exact code. Reference previous_location against previous_candidate when assessing changes. For missing code, locate a real insertion anchor. Never invent ranges or stale hashes.

Evidence uses concise request-local E IDs. The server binds each to immutable content and provenance hashes. Use only IDs in this packet. source_evidence_id must identify a SOURCE entry; source_excerpt, when asserted, must be an exact nonempty substring preserving source whitespace. evidence_id/evidence_excerpt must match supplied text; RDF_FACT permits only one equivalent explicit ground triple with identical RDF terms, lexical forms, datatype and language. No inference, numeric coercion, blank-node equivalence or ontology-wide lookup. A valid reference does not prove the interpretation. Caller admission is an experimental assumption with provenance, not a legal-source quotation or independently certified eligibility.

Decisions: ACCEPT (no issues, all changes supported and prior issues resolved); REJECT (actionable source/schema-backed code issue); UNRESOLVED (material missing information); REQUEST_EVIDENCE (up to three bounded catalog source/schema requests). Unsupported claims, uncertainty and absent evidence must remain explicit. For every material retrieval gap include unchecked {scope: gap_id, material, reason}. Material unchecked scope prevents ACCEPT. Activation/deactivation and full query correctness are separate obligations; resolving scope proves neither arithmetic nor compliance.

For each functional change_id return ONE change_assessments entry, with source support, current/previous locations and reason. If removal_required is true, removal_disposition must be SUPPORTED_REMOVAL, REPLACED, REGRESSION or UNRESOLVED and the reason must assess lost numeric/unit/query/target obligations and any replacement. REGRESSION/UNRESOLVED requires a corresponding issue/change_id; UNRESOLVED requires an unresolved-context issue and decision.

Reconcile exactly the original prior_issues IDs; code edits alone do not resolve an issue. Empty prior_issues requires empty reconciliations. Format feedback does not create accepted issues or authorize repair; the original candidate/prior state and request binding remain unchanged. Echo candidate_version, candidate_sha256 and review_request_id. Correct all listed format errors in a complete response.

Use proposed_path_role PROPERTY for a path ending at the named property, NUMERIC_OPERAND for traversal through that quantity property to the declared numeric predicate. Do not concatenate unrelated owner branches or relabel units as conversion. Vocabulary/domain/range facts do not alone establish ownership or legal eligibility.

4.1.1     Hull regions

For the purpose of this section, the ship's hull is divided into regions as follows (see also Figure
4-3):

Bow region: From the stem to a line parallel to and 0.04∙L aft of the forward borderline of
the part of the hull where the waterlines run parallel to the centerline. For ice classes IA Super
and IA, the overlap over the borderline need not exceed 6 metres, for ice classes IB and IC
this overlap need not exceed 5 metres.

Midbody region: From the aft boundary of the Bow region to a line parallel to and 0.04∙L aft

For ice classes IA Super and IA, the overlap over the borderline need not exceed 6 metres, for
ice classes IB and IC this overlap need not exceed 5 metres.

Stern region: From the aft boundary of the Midbody region to the stern.

L shall be taken as the ship's rule length used by the classification society.
